cues.sky: Night at Knossos Station. Above the dark tube of the telescope: stars, a small red point, a moving point of light, and the Moon.
cues.where: The same sky. Three things could be answering: the red point that is Mars, a satellite crossing the stars, and the Moon.
cues.moon: The telescope closes in on the Moon until it fills the view. Tonight's phase: part of it is in sunlight, part in shadow.
cues.aim: The aiming map: a real photograph of Tranquility Base taken from orbit. A bright dot is Eagle's lower half. Two smaller dots lie just south of it. A crosshair marks where the laser points.
cues.beam: The Earth on the left, the Moon on the right. A pulse of light leaves the Earth. It takes more than a second to cross. A few points of light come back. A clock stops at 2.56 seconds.
cues.found: The Moon fills the view again. A small gold ring marks Tranquility Base, in the Sea of Tranquility.
cues.monologue: The Moon, alone in the dark, very slowly growing in the view.
cues.dim: The lights of the station console go down, one by one.
cues.pulse: The sky above the station. A flash leaves the telescope. Two and a half seconds later, a faint flash answers from the Moon.
